What constitution would you write for a real life country?

A few notes: this important question has a lot of ready-made answers by now. The book https://www.amazon.co.uk/Securities-against-Misrule-Assemblies-Elections/dp/1107649951 is reasonably readable and both comprehensive and interesting. A web search finds a page that seems to be claiming to be the focus of academic work on the subject - http://comparativeconstitutionsproject.org/

You're never starting from a complete unknown, and there might not be one best answer. You would be starting from a country that has some previous constitution and whose people expect something in particular and are used to behaving in a particular way. Even if you're the head of an occupying army, you'll do better with working with what you have got, not imposing something completely alien.

I favour small, reversible, changes done one at a time in a way that allows people to work out what the consequences of their actions really are. So I would almost never suggest imposing a new constitution, as opposed to making incremental changes to an existing one. For example, I see the Economist Magazine is very keen on limiting heads of state to two terms. That's a good idea that more countries should have.

This stuff is tricky - for example your point "2-Ensure citizens have their basic needs met". What is a basic need? I grew up perfectly happily in a house without a fridge, central heating, or (except for the last two years) a telephone. When I was working in London a few years later I heard that it was supposedly a national disgrace that there were people in London who didn't have central heating. What is a basic need? Does your constitution guarantee free food for everybody? I happen to need to wear 300 pounds (so rather more dollars) worth of glasses to see properly, and I get these changed every year because my eyesight continues to deteriorate. Does your constitution guarantee me that?
It'd largely be the same as the US Constitution, but with the 17th Amendment excluded, and the 14th Amendment written in a way that clearly bans the anchor-baby loophole.
